Four rounds are typically necessary for triples at TV 1/4

Draw one uniform permutation PP on q=2nq=2^n bit strings and apply the same PP after a fresh uniform XOR key in every round. At every fixed total variation threshold 0<ϵ<1/30<\epsilon<1/3, the worst-start ordered-triple mixing time is exactly four rounds with probability tending to one. For 1/2<ϵ<11/2<\epsilon<1 it is exactly three. The behavior between these two ranges, including the endpoints, remains open. These conclusions combine a computer-assisted calculation after three rounds with the four-round upper bound. Published priority for the random-table result remains unverified. Four-round proof

Two keys leave empty cells

A triple up to translation has a shape given by its two differences from one designated point. There are m=(q−1)(q−2)m=(q-1)(q-2) shapes. Write Ds(P)D_s(P) for the distance to uniform after two shape steps starting from shape ss. This equals the distance on actual ordered triples after three cipher rounds. The final uniform key spreads the first point uniformly within its shape, and the final application of PP preserves total variation. Reduction to shapes

For fixed P,sP,s there are L=q2L=q^2 equally probable ordered two-key paths. Independently choose a uniform target shape YY and let ZZ count the paths ending there. A missing target contributes 1/m1/m to the total deficit from uniform. A target hit exactly once contributes 1/m−1/L1/m-1/L. Every other target contributes zero to the deficit. Consequently

0≤Ds(P)−Ms(P)≤1−m/L=O(1/q).0\le D_s(P)-M_s(P)\le 1-m/L=O(1/q).

Computing the factorial moments

Choose jj independent uniform key pairs and run their paths from one starting triple. Let EjE_j be the event that the key pairs are pairwise distinct and their endpoints have the same shape. Summing over the LjL^j ordered choices of key pairs gives

𝔼P,Y[(Z)j]=q2jmPr(Ej).\mathbb E_{P,Y}[(Z)_j]=\frac{q^{2j}}{m}\Pr(E_j).

The factor 1/m1/m is the chance that the independent target equals the common endpoint. For j=1j=1, this already gives q2/mq^2/m. For j=2,3j=2,3, the following finite enumeration gives

Pr(Ej)=q−2(j−1)(1+O(1/q)).\Pr(E_j)=q^{-2(j-1)}(1+O(1/q)).

Represent the starting triple as (0,a,b)(0,a,b) for two fixed independent binary vectors. Any other triple reduces to this one by translation and a linear change of coordinates. Conjugating a uniform PP preserves its law. Evaluate all six calls to PP on each path, retaining the input addresses and replies shared across all paths. Each address is a key XOR either an initial point or a previous reply.

Consider one exact pattern of equal addresses with kk distinct addresses. Give their outputs kk variables. Past addresses coincide precisely as prescribed and the kk outputs must be distinct. Add the two vector equations per further path that equate its endpoint differences to the first path's. For every pair of paths, require at least one of its two keys to differ. Given an assignment satisfying these conditions, a uniform table realizes the assigned outputs with probability 1/(q)k1/(q)_k. The keys contribute q−2jq^{-2j}, even when their later query addresses depend on earlier replies. The exact contribution of the pattern is the number of admissible assignments divided by q2j(q)kq^{2j}(q)_k.

Let ee be the rank of the vector equations in the 2j+k2j+k variables. In a consistent pattern their solution space has q2j+k−eq^{2j+k-e} points. A nonzero linear combination of a,ba,b cannot be forced to zero. Any required inequality between addresses or outputs either holds identically, is impossible, or rules out just a 1/q1/q fraction. Identical key pairs require both component equalities. If both are forced, discard the pattern. Otherwise the forbidden joint event is empty or lies inside a proper affine subspace of relative size at most 1/q1/q. There are finitely many restrictions, so a consistent pattern has weight q−e(1+O(1/q))q^{-e}(1+O(1/q)) as qq grows.

The checker searches the exact patterns as follows.

  1. Encode each key, reply, and the constants a,ba,b by distinct bits. Keep the full binary linear span of all imposed equations. It contains at most 16 expressions for j≤3j\le3 through the required rank 2(j−1)2(j-1). An address equality is forced precisely when its XOR belongs to the span.
  2. A forced repeated address reuses its unique value. Otherwise branch on a hit to each distinct earlier address and one fresh address. The fresh branch records all inequalities that distinguish its input and output from earlier ones. These cases are exhaustive and disjoint.
  3. Add the two endpoint equations of each subsequent path as soon as the corresponding replies are available. After extending the equation span, reject a contradictory constant, a violated inequality, or a forced identical key pair. Further equations and fresh variables cannot lower the existing rank.
  4. Count terminal paths through rank 2(j−1)2(j-1). All higher-rank terminal paths combined contribute O(q−2(j−1)−1)O(q^{-2(j-1)-1}) because the number of equality patterns of at most 18 calls is a fixed constant.

At each order the unique surviving pattern has distinct addresses throughout. This proves the probability estimate and all three factorial moment identities. An independent computation allowing repeated key pairs gives limiting ordinary moments 1,2,51,2,5, agreeing with the factorial moments. The standard-library certificate reproduces the table. From one start to every start

Transposing two images of PP changes a one-step shape row in TV by at most 6/q6/q. Only keys bringing one of the three points to one of the exchanged inputs can affect the row. A coupling over two steps therefore bounds the change of Ds(P)D_s(P) by 12/q12/q. Expose the uniform permutation one image at a time. Completions for two possible images can be paired by one transposition. Azuma's inequality bounds the two-sided tail at distance tt from the mean by 2exp(−qt2/288)2\exp(-qt^2/288). A union bound over the mm starting shapes now gives, simultaneously for all ss,

13−OK(logqq)≤Ds(P)≤12+OK(logqq)\frac13-O_K\!\left(\sqrt{\frac{\log q}{q}}\right) \le D_s(P)\le \frac12+O_K\!\left(\sqrt{\frac{\log q}{q}}\right)

with probability 1−OK(q−K)1-O_K(q^{-K}) for every fixed K>0K>0. After two full cipher rounds a starting triple has at most qq shapes in the corresponding one-step distribution, so its TV is at least 1−q/m1-q/m. After four full rounds the worst-start distance tends to zero with high probability. These facts give the stated threshold times. At any fixed threshold strictly inside either range, the same concentration estimates with constant tt give an exponentially small exceptional probability. Four-round concentration
